title: Verified regret matching and finite-time equilibrium computation
summary: For finite nonempty action sets and unit-interval full-information payoffs, regret matching and regret matching+ have cumulative external regret at most the square root of the product of the number of actions and the horizon, against every fixed pure or mixed comparator. In finite two-player zero-sum matrix games, simultaneous self-play gives an explicit finite-time approximate Nash guarantee for uniformly averaged strategies. A finite-vector implementation is proved to reproduce the abstract averages. Square-root-free accuracy budgets and finite rational payoff inequalities certify…
